discovery: Prediction and observational discovery of magnetars, neutron stars powered by ultrastrong magnetic fields

nominees.name: Robert C. Duncan
nominees.affiliation: University of Texas at Austin, USA

nominees.name: Christopher Thompson
nominees.affiliation: Canadian Institute for Theoretical Astrophysics, University of Toronto, Canada

motivation: Duncan and Thompson predicted in 1992 that neutron stars born with magnetic fields of 10^14-10^15 gauss, a thousand times stronger than ordinary pulsars, would be powered by magnetic-field decay and would emit bursts of X-rays and gamma rays. In 1998 Kouveliotou and collaborators measured the spin period and rapid spin-down of the soft gamma repeater SGR 1806-20 with RXTE, directly confirming a magnetic field of ~10^15 gauss and establishing magnetars as a new class of star. This work revealed the strongest magnetic fields in the universe, where quantum electrodynamics operates in regimes impossible to reach in the laboratory, and explains soft gamma repeaters, anomalous X-ray pulsars, giant flares and, as shown by the 2020 detection of a fast radio burst from SGR 1935+2154, at least some fast radio bursts. It is a clear example of tightly linked theory and high-energy observation transforming our view of compact objects.
